title: Overfitting in neural networks
prompt: As a flower image classifier trains, its training loss keeps falling but its validation loss rises after epoch 8. What is likely happening, and what are two ways to respond?
objective: Recognise overfitting in learning curves and explain two practical mitigations.
expected_scope: Diagnose the curve pattern and explain two remedies such as early stopping, a smaller model or regularisation.
hint: Consider changing when training stops or how much detail the model can fit.
reference_explanation: The network is likely overfitting, because extra training improves its fit to training images while worsening performance on held-out images. Early stopping can restore the weights from an epoch with good validation performance. A smaller network, weight regularisation or dropout can reduce its ability to rely on training-specific patterns. Check the revised model on held-out data.

criteria.description: Explains the loss gap as evidence of fitting training data at the expense of validation performance.
Names a sensible mitigation and explains how it addresses overfitting.
Names and explains a second distinct mitigation.

critical_misconceptions: Claiming that the model is underfitting solely because the validation loss is rising.
